mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances following a FEDFUNDS increase > 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over a 3-month period indicates growing demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic expansion and typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances following a 3-month increase in HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% over a 3-month period signals a tightening labor market, which is typically associated with increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances following a UNRATE decrease > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over a 3-month period signals increased economic output, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances following an INDPRO increase > 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over a 3-month period signals a strong consumer-driven economy, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increase > 1% and UNRATE decrease > 0.3% in 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances following the joint increase in RSAFS and decrease in UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 2% over a 6-month period signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the Federal Reserve is expected to tighten monetary policy.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances following a CPIAUCSL increase > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 over a 3-month period signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances following a PAYEMS decrease > 100,000.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in real GDP (GDPC1) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over a 6-month period signals a robust economic expansion, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increase > 1% and UNRATE decrease > 0.5% in 6 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances following the joint increase in GDPC1 and decrease in UNRATE.
